Round 14 — the whole page, five compositions

Round 13 settled one column (D161). This round proposes the page, because the operator asked: why two graphics in one place, can they go elsewhere, and what would make the landing page more interesting? Five compositions of the same built page, each photographed whole, at one display factor, from the load that produced its numbers (D160). Nothing here touches src/: applying a composition is a separate commit set, after the ruling.

Question 1 — which composition?

Answer in letters (e.g. “1C”), and say if a mix is meant.

A — the page as it stands. Round 13 option C, shipped today: text left, plate-over-mark right, no art below the fold. The incumbent, and the baseline every other row is a delta from. Its measured weakness is not the hero, it is the mid-page: 9 empty runs over 25.1% of the page, and a 1606px `bg-panel` section that carries no art.

B — the drawing opens the page. Byrne before the headline. The hero stops being two columns and becomes a stack: a full-width band of the engraving above the fold, then the words, then the mark at its natural 240px. This is how Byrne’s own books open — the figure, then the proposition. Costs the most colour of any option (the widest window on the leaf the page is allowed one of) and the most resolution shortfall, because 1192px of band is painted from a 1024px scan.

C — a horizon in the middle of the page. Keep the hero exactly as ruled, and put the line-work plate full-width between the club’s reasons and the schedule — where the page is emptiest by measurement. 1910 geometry is colourless, so this buys a horizon for almost no colour (record 0023 measured the 1910 plate at 0.000% at chroma >= 0.08) and it sits in a section that already pays for py-16 of padding.

D — one graphic per place, mark at the foot. The answer to "can they go elsewhere": yes, and each place gets one job. The hero column holds only the plate, at the column’s full height (574px, so the widest honest window on the leaf the column already pays for); the identity mark moves out of the fold and closes the page in the ink footer, where it has to be repainted to survive a dark ground: measured in this round, moving it with only its ink strokes repainted left the gold paths at **2.5** against ink — under the 3.0 graphic bar (D101), twelve FAILs — so the option includes `--color-gold-on-ink` (5.80 on ink), the token the system already has; PS-3 takes the line-work plate; and the schedule notice takes the 323x110 thumb the operator ruled (a). The art-forward page.

E — the plate on an ink spine. The boldest look on the table: the hero’s media column becomes a dark band that runs to the page’s right edge, so the engraving hangs on ink like a print in a hallway and the footer and the hero share one ground. It changes the page’s darkest surface, not just its art, so it is the option most likely to move the ground and contrast gates — which is why it is measured rather than admired.

The five pages, one scale

Same viewport (390), same factor, whole document — top to bottom. This is the comparison: rhythm, weight, and where the page puts its one coloured thing.

The heroes, closer

What the measurements say

  • Colour: the cheapest page is two-horizons at 0.260% of pixels at chroma ≥ 0.08, the richest is art-owns-the-top at 5.034%; the shipped page is 0.274%. One coloured slot is the ruling (D149-1b/2b), so this column is the budget being spent.
  • Page height: every option's cost is printed at all four widths, because the desktop column lied once — round 13's option C was “+0” at 1240 and **+314px at 390**. The tallest here is one-graphic-per-place at 6552 (+6552).
  • Emptiness — the thing this page is actually short of, and the metric most easily misled. At 390 the shipped page has 13 empty runs covering 20.8% of its height, which is 1284 px of unmarked vertical space. Percentages flatter a page that grows, so compare the pixels: as-shipped 1284px (20.8%), art-owns-the-top 1284px (20.8%), two-horizons 1282px (20.6%), one-graphic-per-place 1389px (21.2%), ink-spine 1392px (21.8%).
  • Gates: every option is green on `check:render` at 1240/640/390/320 — these are compositions to choose between, not breakage to fix.
  • Resolution: the archive ladder stops at 1024px (record 0023), so band-hero paints 1192px from a 688px scan (**1.73× upscale**); band-mid paints 1176px from a 698px scan (**1.68× upscale**). A full-bleed band is a decision about a bigger scan, not only about layout.

How this was made

npm run round14 (design/round14.mjs): mutate dist/client/index.html per option — a <style> block, DOM moves, plates planted as data URIs through design/grill/plate-crop.mjs, the same recipe that built src/assets/photos/hero.png — then run the gates CI runs. Options are defined in design/grill/round14-options.mjs; this file is generated from design/grill/round14/report.json and throws on a missing lookup. A design round, not a gate: it runs in no CI.
